csv-to-pdf.title: CSV to PDF — convert a spreadsheet to a PDF table, free
csv-to-pdf.description: Convert CSV to a formatted PDF table in your browser, with a repeating header and Cyrillic support. Nothing is uploaded.
csv-to-pdf.intro: Make a CSV printable. The result is a real table with a header that repeats on every page, not a screenshot, and the text stays selectable.

howTo.step1: Add the CSV file.
howTo.step2: Choose page size, orientation and font size.
howTo.step3: Press Create PDF and download it.

faq.q1: My table is too wide. What do I do?
faq.a1: Switch to landscape, or A3 for a very wide table, and drop the font size. The tool suggests landscape once there are more than eight columns.
faq.a2: Yes. The embedded font covers Russian and Uzbek Cyrillic, so nothing comes out as empty boxes.
faq.q3: Is the header repeated on every page?
faq.a3: Yes, if the first row is marked as a header. On a long table that is the difference between a usable printout and an unreadable one.
faq.q4: Can I select the text in the PDF?
faq.a4: Yes. Every cell is real text, so the PDF can be searched and copied from.

excel-to-pdf.name: Excel to PDF
excel-to-pdf.short: Print a spreadsheet sheet as a PDF table.
excel-to-pdf.title: Excel to PDF — convert XLSX to PDF online, free
excel-to-pdf.description: Convert an Excel sheet to a formatted PDF table in your browser, with a repeating header and Cyrillic support. Nothing is uploaded.
excel-to-pdf.intro: Turn a sheet into a clean PDF table without opening Excel, and without uploading a spreadsheet that may hold prices, salaries or client names.

howTo.step1: Add the .xlsx file.
howTo.step2: Choose the sheet, then page size and orientation.
howTo.step3: Press Create PDF and download it.

faq.q1: Does it look like Excel's own print output?
faq.a1: No. This lays out a clean table from the cell values — it does not reproduce Excel's fonts, colours, borders, merged cells or print areas. For an exact copy, print to PDF from Excel.
faq.a2: They are not included. Only cell values are converted.
faq.a3: The first, unless you pick another. One sheet per PDF.
faq.a4: You get the displayed value, which is what you would want on a printout — the date as shown, not the number behind it.

pdf-grayscale.name: Grayscale PDF
pdf-grayscale.short: Make a PDF print in black and white.
pdf-grayscale.title: Grayscale PDF — convert a PDF to black and white online, free
pdf-grayscale.description: Convert a PDF to grayscale in your browser without rasterising it. The text stays selectable and the file barely grows. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-grayscale.intro: Turn a colour PDF grey for printing. Unlike tools that render every page to an image, this keeps the text as text — so the file stays small, searchable and sharp.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF.
howTo.step2: Press Convert to grayscale.
howTo.step3: Download the result and print it.

faq.q1: Is the colour actually removed?
faq.a1: No, and this is the important part. The colour is switched off for display and printing, but the original colour data is still inside the file. Do not use this to redact colour-coded information — use it to save ink.
faq.q2: Why not just print in black and white?
faq.a2: You can, when you control the printer. This is for when you do not: sending a file to a print shop, a colleague, or a system that charges by the colour page.
faq.a3: Yes. The page is not converted to an image, so text remains selectable and searchable, and the file size hardly changes.
faq.q4: Will every viewer show it in grey?
faq.a4: Every current viewer and printer will. The effect relies on a standard PDF blend mode, and a very old viewer that ignores blend modes would show the original colours.

scan-to-pdf.name: Photos to scanned PDF
scan-to-pdf.short: Turn phone photos of a document into a clean PDF.
scan-to-pdf.title: Photo to PDF scanner — free online, no app needed
scan-to-pdf.description: Turn photos of a document into a clean, scan-like PDF in your browser. Whitens the paper and darkens the text. Nothing is uploaded.
scan-to-pdf.intro: Photograph a document with your phone and get a PDF that looks scanned rather than photographed. The clean-up pass whitens the paper and darkens the text, which is what separates this from simply putting photos in a PDF.

howTo.step1: Add your photos — all of them at once.
howTo.step2: Drag them into page order and choose a clean-up mode.
howTo.step3: Press Create PDF and download it.

faq.q1: What does Enhance actually do?
faq.a1: It finds where the paper and the ink sit in the image's brightness range and stretches that range to full black and white. That is what turns a grey, unevenly lit photo into something that reads as a scan.
faq.q2: When should I keep the colour?
faq.a2: For anything where colour carries meaning — a stamp, a coloured signature, a certificate. Enhance is for printed black text on white paper.
faq.a3: Not yet. Hold the phone parallel to the page and fill the frame; the clean-up handles lighting, not perspective.
faq.a4: No. Everything happens on your device, which is the point when you are photographing a passport or a contract.

pdf-to-jpg.name: PDF to JPG
pdf-to-jpg.short: Turn PDF pages into JPG images.
pdf-to-jpg.title: PDF to JPG — convert PDF pages to images online, free
pdf-to-jpg.description: Free online tool that converts PDF pages to JPG images in your browser, with a page-by-page preview to choose which ones. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-to-jpg.intro: Turn some or all pages of a PDF into JPG images. Pick the pages visually, choose a size and quality, and get a single image back or a .zip when more than one page is selected.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF and wait for the page previews to load.
howTo.step2: Click the pages you want, or type a range instead.
howTo.step3: Choose a size and quality, then press Convert.

faq.q1: Why does it sometimes give one file and sometimes a .zip?
faq.a1: A single selected page comes back as one JPG, ready to use directly. Select more than one and they are bundled into a .zip, since the site can only offer one download at a time.
faq.a2: Medium (1600px) reads well on a screen and prints acceptably. Large (2500px) is for printing or further editing; small (800px) is enough for a thumbnail or a quick preview.
faq.q3: Does this work on a scanned PDF?
faq.a3: Yes — a scan is just a picture already, so this reproduces it as-is at the size you choose.
faq.q4: Is a very long PDF a problem?
faq.a4: Pages beyond a few hundred skip the visual previews to stay responsive, but the page-range field still selects them by number, and conversion itself runs in the background so the page does not freeze.

pdf-to-text.name: PDF to text
pdf-to-text.short: Pull the text out of a PDF.
pdf-to-text.title: PDF to text — extract text from a PDF online, free
pdf-to-text.description: Free online tool that extracts the text layer from a PDF, entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-to-text.intro: Get the plain text out of a PDF that already has one — a document exported from Word, a report, an invoice. Runs in the browser, so nothing about the file leaves your device.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF.
howTo.step2: Press Extract text and wait for every page to be read.
howTo.step3: Copy the result or save it as a .txt file.

faq.q1: Why is the result empty?
faq.a1: The PDF has no text layer — it is a scan or a photo saved as a PDF, which is a picture of text rather than text. Use the image-to-text (OCR) tool instead; it reads the picture directly.
faq.a2: No, only the words do, roughly in reading order. Columns, tables and headers and footers are not reconstructed — this is for getting the text out, not a layout converter.
faq.a3: Yes, as long as the PDF embeds its fonts properly, which is true of the vast majority of PDFs produced by Word, Excel or a browser's own PDF export.
faq.a4: No. It is read and processed entirely in your browser.

pdf-compress.name: Compress PDF
pdf-compress.short: Shrink a PDF by recompressing its images, without touching the text.
pdf-compress.title: Compress PDF — shrink file size online, free, text stays searchable
pdf-compress.description: Free online tool that shrinks a PDF by recompressing the images inside it. Text and layout are left completely untouched, so the result stays selectable and searchable. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-compress.intro: Most oversized PDFs are oversized because of the photos or scanned pages inside them, not the text. This finds those images and recompresses them — the text stays exactly as it was, still selectable and searchable, which a render-and-rebuild compressor can't promise.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF.
howTo.step2: Pick a compression level.
howTo.step3: Press Compress PDF and download the result.

faq.q1: Why does it say there's nothing to compress?
faq.a1: That means the PDF has no images it can confidently recompress — a text-only document, for instance, which is already small. Rather than rasterise the whole page to manufacture a smaller file (which would break the text), it says so plainly.
faq.q2: Will my document still look right?
faq.a2: Yes. Layout, fonts and every other piece of content are untouched — only the compressed image data inside is replaced with a smaller version.
faq.q3: Does the text stay selectable afterwards?
faq.a3: Yes, completely. Nothing about the text layer changes. This is the entire reason this tool works the way it does rather than rendering pages to pictures.
faq.a4: Anything it isn't fully confident is safe to touch — images already using an indexed or unusual colour space, or ones so small that recompressing them wouldn't help. It only acts where it can be sure of the result.

pdf-compare.name: Compare PDFs
pdf-compare.short: See exactly what changed between two versions of a PDF.
pdf-compare.title: Compare PDF files — see the differences online, free
pdf-compare.description: Free online tool that compares two PDFs page by page and shows exactly what text changed. Runs entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-compare.intro: Add two versions of a document and see, page by page, which ones are identical, which changed, and which were added or removed — with the exact words that differ highlighted on the pages that changed.

howTo.step1: Add the earlier version as Document A and the newer one as Document B.
howTo.step2: Press Compare.
howTo.step3: Open any page marked "Changed" to see exactly which words differ, side by side with both pages.

faq.q1: What counts as "changed"?
faq.a1: The text content differs in a way that isn't just whitespace. A page reformatted with identical wording reads as identical; a single word swapped reads as changed.
faq.q2: Does it compare images or just text?
faq.a2: Text drives the changed/identical decision, since that answers "what changed" directly and works on documents of any length without rendering every page. Pages flagged as changed also show real thumbnails from both documents side by side, so a visual difference is still one click away.
faq.q3: What if the two PDFs have different page counts?
faq.a3: Pages past the end of the shorter document are marked "Added" or "Removed" rather than forced into a false comparison against nothing.
faq.a4: No. Both are read and compared entirely in your browser.

pdf-annotate.name: Annotate PDF
pdf-annotate.short: Highlight and add short notes directly on a PDF.
pdf-annotate.title: Annotate PDF — highlight and add notes online, free
pdf-annotate.description: Free online tool to highlight text and add short notes on a PDF, drawn directly on the rendered page. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-annotate.intro: Mark up a PDF the way you would with a highlighter and sticky notes on paper — drag to highlight, click to drop a short note — right on the actual page, then bake it all in as one file to send back.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF and move to the page you want to mark up.
howTo.step2: Drag to highlight an area, or switch to Note and click to place a short comment.
howTo.step3: Repeat across as many pages as you need, then press Add annotations.

faq.q1: Can this hide or remove information?
faq.a1: No — everything here is drawn on top of the page, and the original content underneath is completely untouched and still there. If you need to permanently remove sensitive content, use the separate Redact tool, which is built differently precisely because this one isn't safe for that.
faq.q2: Why can notes only use Latin letters?
faq.a2: The fonts built into the PDF format can't draw Cyrillic without embedding a much larger font file. A note using other characters is skipped rather than silently turning into empty boxes — everything else you added still goes through.
faq.q3: Can I undo one highlight without starting over?
faq.a3: Yes — each mark on the current page has its own Remove button, and "Clear this page" drops everything on just that page.
faq.a4: No. Rendering and everything else happens in your browser.

pdf-redact.name: Redact PDF
pdf-redact.short: Permanently black out sensitive content — safely.
pdf-redact.title: Redact PDF — permanently remove sensitive content, free
pdf-redact.description: Free online tool that permanently removes sensitive content from a PDF page, not just covers it. The redacted page becomes a flattened image, so nothing is left behind the black box to recover. Nothing is uploaded.
pdf-redact.intro: Black out sensitive information the way it actually needs to be done: the page is flattened to an image with the black box painted directly onto it, so there is nothing hidden underneath left to select, copy or extract. Read the notice above before using this on anything sensitive.

howTo.step1: Add the PDF and move to the page with sensitive content.
howTo.step2: Drag a box over each area to remove.
howTo.step3: Press Redact and download the result.

faq.q1: Is this actually safe, or just a black box on top?
faq.a1: It's the real thing. A black box drawn on top of live text — which is what many quick tools do — still leaves that text selectable and copyable underneath. This instead turns the whole redacted page into a flattened image before anything is saved, so there is no text layer left behind the box at all.
faq.a2: A redacted page's text is no longer selectable or searchable afterwards, because it is no longer text — it's a picture of the page with the sensitive area removed. That is the honest cost of doing this safely, not a limitation to work around.
faq.q3: What happens to pages I don't mark?
faq.a3: Nothing at all. Only pages with at least one redaction box are touched; every other page keeps its real, original text.
faq.q4: Can I undo a redaction after downloading?
faq.a4: No — once applied and downloaded, it's permanent, by design. Double-check every box before pressing Redact, and keep your original file if you might need the removed content again.

image-crop.name: Crop image
image-crop.short: Cut a picture down to the part you want.
image-crop.title: Crop Image — cut a photo online, free, no upload
image-crop.description: Free online image cropper. Drag the borders to choose exactly what to keep, then save it. Runs in your browser — the picture is never uploaded.
image-crop.intro: Add a picture and drag on it to choose what to keep. Pull any border or corner to adjust the frame, drag the middle to move it, and everything outside stays dimmed so you can see what you are keeping.

howTo.step1: Add the image you want to crop.
howTo.step2: Drag on it to frame the part you want, then adjust the borders.
howTo.step3: Press Crop image and download the result.

faq.q1: Can I crop to an exact size?
faq.a1: Yes. Frame roughly what you want, then type the exact width and height below the picture — the crop is saved at that size. Leave the numbers alone to keep the selection at its original resolution.
faq.a2: Yes, once: the selected area is drawn and saved again in the same format. A JPG stays a JPG and a PNG stays a PNG, and quality is kept high, but a JPG will lose a little on any re-save — that is unavoidable when cutting a picture.
faq.q3: Does it work on phone photos?
faq.a3: Yes, including HEIC from an iPhone, which most croppers refuse. Touch works the same as a mouse: drag to frame, drag a border to adjust.
faq.a4: No. The crop happens inside your browser, on your own device. Nothing is sent to a server, which is also why it works with the tab offline once the page has loaded.

jpg-to-webp.name: JPG to WebP
jpg-to-webp.short: Convert photos to WebP, the smaller web format.
jpg-to-webp.title: JPG to WebP — convert images online, free
jpg-to-webp.description: Free online JPG to WebP converter. WebP files are typically 25–35% smaller than JPG at the same quality. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
jpg-to-webp.intro: Add a JPG and convert it to WebP. At the same visual quality WebP usually saves a quarter to a third of the bytes, which is why it is the format of choice for websites.

howTo.step1: Add the JPG you want to convert.
howTo.step2: Set the quality — 80 to 90 suits photographs.
howTo.step3: Press Convert and download the WebP.

faq.q1: Why use WebP at all?
faq.a1: It compresses better than JPG — usually 25 to 35% smaller at the same visible quality — so pages load faster and use less of a visitor's data. Every current browser supports it.
faq.a2: Not at sensible quality settings. WebP is lossy like JPG, so converting means one more round of compression; at 85 or above the difference is invisible on a photograph.
faq.q3: Can I put WebP on a website?
faq.a3: Yes. Every browser released in the last several years displays WebP. Only very old software struggles, which is why some sites still keep a JPG fallback.
faq.a4: Converting to WebP needs the browser to have a WebP encoder. Safari has had one since version 14; if yours is older the tool will say so rather than hand you a mislabelled file.

png-to-webp.name: PNG to WebP
png-to-webp.title: PNG to WebP — convert images online, free
png-to-webp.description: Free online PNG to WebP converter. Keeps transparency and usually produces a much smaller file. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
png-to-webp.intro: Add a PNG and convert it to WebP. Transparency is kept, and screenshots and graphics usually come out far smaller than the PNG they started as.

howTo.step1: Add the PNG you want to convert.
howTo.step2: Choose a quality level.
howTo.step3: Press Convert and download the WebP.

faq.q1: Is transparency kept?
faq.a1: Yes. WebP supports an alpha channel just as PNG does, so a logo with a transparent background stays transparent.
faq.q2: How much smaller will it be?
faq.a2: For screenshots and graphics, often several times smaller. The saving is largest on images with photographic areas and smallest on flat-colour icons, which PNG already handles well.
faq.a3: WebP here is lossy, so fine detail is approximated — invisible at high quality on most graphics, but if you need pixel-exact output keep the PNG.
faq.a4: Safari has encoded WebP since version 14. On anything older the tool refuses rather than quietly handing back a PNG with a .webp name.

image-rotate.name: Rotate image
image-rotate.short: Turn a picture the right way up, or mirror it.
image-rotate.title: Rotate Image — turn or flip a photo online, free
image-rotate.description: Free online image rotator. Turn a photo 90°, 180° or 270°, or mirror it across or down, and save it. Runs in your browser — the picture is never uploaded.
image-rotate.intro: Add a picture and use the buttons to turn it a quarter turn at a time or mirror it. The preview updates as you go and is exactly what gets saved, so a sideways phone photo takes two clicks to fix.

howTo.step1: Add the picture that is facing the wrong way.
howTo.step2: Turn it left or right until it looks right, and mirror it if you need to.
howTo.step3: Press Save rotated image and download the result.

faq.q1: Why is my photo sideways in the first place?
faq.a1: Phones store the picture as the sensor saw it and add a note saying which way the phone was held. Apps that ignore that note show it sideways. This tool reads the note, applies it, and then saves the picture actually turned the right way — so it looks correct everywhere afterwards.
faq.a2: A quarter turn moves whole pixels, so nothing is blurred or resampled. A JPG is saved again at high quality, which costs a very small amount on any re-save; a PNG or WebP loses nothing at all.
faq.q3: What is the difference between rotating and flipping?
faq.a3: Rotating turns the picture. Flipping mirrors it, the way a mirror reverses left and right — useful for a selfie that came out backwards, or for scanned film that was fed in the wrong way round. Text in a flipped picture reads backwards, which is the quick way to tell them apart.
faq.a4: No. The turn happens inside your browser, on your own device. Nothing is sent to a server, which is also why it keeps working with the tab offline once the page has loaded.

image-metadata.name: Remove EXIF data
image-metadata.short: See what your photo says about you, then take it out.

image-metadata.intro: Add a photo and see exactly what it is carrying: where it was taken, which camera took it, that camera's serial number and the second the shutter fired. Then remove all of it in one click. The pixels are copied through untouched, so the picture is not re-compressed.

howTo.step1: Add a photo straight from a camera or phone.
howTo.step2: Read what it found — the location is usually the surprising part.
howTo.step3: Press Remove all of it and download the clean file.

faq.q1: What is EXIF data?
faq.a1: A block of notes the camera writes inside the picture file. It normally holds the make and model, the exposure settings, the date and time to the second, often the camera's serial number, and — if location was on — the GPS position where you stood, accurate to a few metres. None of it shows in the picture; all of it travels with the file.
faq.q2: Does removing it change the picture?
faq.a2: No. The compressed image data is copied across byte for byte and only the note segments are cut out, so there is no second round of JPEG compression and no quality loss at all. The file just gets smaller.
faq.a3: Anything that affects how the picture looks: the colour profile, transparency, and animation frames. Removing a colour profile would shift the colours, so it stays. Everything else — location, camera, serial numbers, dates, editing history, comments — goes.
faq.q4: Do social networks not already strip this?
faq.a4: Most do, which is why people assume it is never there. The risk is everything that does not go through one: a photo emailed, sent as a file on a messenger, put on your own website, or attached to a marketplace listing keeps the full set of notes.
faq.a5: No — and on this tool that matters more than most. The file is read and rewritten inside your browser, on your own device. A site that asked you to upload a photo to have its location removed would already have the location.

image-redact.name: Blur or pixelate
image-redact.short: Cover a face, a plate or an address before you share a picture.
image-redact.title: Blur Image — hide faces and plates online, free, no upload
image-redact.description: Free online tool to blur or pixelate part of a picture. Drag over a face, a number plate or an address and save it covered. Runs in your browser — the picture is never uploaded.
image-redact.intro: Drag over anything you do not want shared — a face, a number plate, a house number, a name on a document — and it is covered as you draw. Cover as many areas as you like, then save. The covering is applied to the picture itself, so there is nothing underneath to recover.

howTo.step1: Add the picture you want to share.
howTo.step2: Drag over each thing you want hidden.
howTo.step3: Press Save hidden version and download it.

faq.q1: Can the covered part be recovered?
faq.a1: Not from the saved file. The pixels under each box are thrown away and replaced before the picture is written, so there is no original hiding underneath. This is the difference between this and drawing a shape over a photo in a document — there the picture is still intact under the shape, and moving the shape reveals it.
faq.q2: Blur or pixelate — which is safer?
faq.a2: Pixelate, which is why it is the default. A light blur can sometimes be partly undone by software that knows what blur was applied; flattening an area into a handful of flat blocks throws the detail away outright. Whichever you choose, push the strength up: at the top setting a face is a few squares.
faq.q3: Does the rest of the picture change?
faq.a3: Only the areas you drew are touched. The picture is re-saved in the same format at high quality, so a JPG gives up a very small amount everywhere as any re-save does; a PNG or WebP gives up nothing.
faq.q4: Does it remove the location and camera details too?
faq.a4: Re-saving drops them as a side effect, so the file you download has no EXIF block. If you want to see what was in there before removing it — the coordinates are usually the surprise — use the Remove EXIF data tool, which shows you the list.
faq.a5: No. Drawing and saving both happen inside your browser, on your own device. A picture you are covering something in is exactly the picture you would least want to upload to a stranger's server, and you are not being asked to.

image-passport.name: Passport photo
image-passport.short: Cut a photo to 3×4, 3.5×4.5 or any document size, ready to print.
image-passport.title: Passport Photo Maker — 3×4, 35×45 mm online, free
image-passport.description: Free passport and ID photo maker. Crop to 30×40, 35×45 mm, 2×2 in and other document sizes at 300 DPI, and lay several out on one 10×15 cm sheet to print. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
image-passport.intro: Pick the size your form asks for, position the frame over the face using the head guides, and get either one photo at the exact millimetres or a sheet with several copies laid out for printing. A print shop charges the same for a 10×15 print whether it carries one photo or eight.

howTo.step1: Add a photo taken against a plain, light wall.
howTo.step2: Pick the size your form asks for and line the head up between the dashed guides.
howTo.step3: Choose a sheet to print or a single photo, then download it.

faq.q1: Which size do I need?
faq.a1: 35 × 45 mm is the international standard: passports, Schengen and UK visas, and most application forms outside the CIS. 30 × 40 mm is the usual size for documents across the CIS, and 35 × 40 mm turns up on some Uzbek forms. The USA and India want a 2 × 2 inch square. If the form names millimetres, match them exactly — this is one of the things that gets photos returned.
faq.q2: What are the dashed lines for?
faq.a2: They mark where the head goes. Nearly every standard says the same thing: the head fills about three quarters of the frame, sits slightly below the top edge, and is centred. Line the top of the hair up with the upper line and the chin with the lower one, and the proportions are right. Getting this wrong is the most common reason a photo is rejected — far more common than the size being off.
faq.a3: It is what print shops expect, and the number the photo is actually saved at: a 35 × 45 mm photo comes out as 413 × 531 pixels. Fewer pixels than that and the print looks soft; more is wasted on paper this small. If you are uploading to a visa portal instead of printing, the same file works, and the Compress image tool will bring it under a size limit if the portal sets one.
faq.q4: Can it make the background white?
faq.a4: No — and no browser tool can do it well enough to trust for a document. Take the photo against a plain, evenly lit light wall, with no shadow behind the head. That is what the rules ask for anyway, and it is far more reliable than anything that cuts you out afterwards.
faq.q5: How do I print the sheet?
faq.a5: Send the 10 × 15 cm file to any print shop or photo kiosk as a normal photo print, or print the A4 version at home on photo paper at 100% scale, with no fitting or shrinking. Cut along the thin grey lines. Make sure the printer is not set to fit the page, or every photo will come out slightly the wrong size.

image-social.name: Social media sizes
image-social.short: Cut a picture to the exact size YouTube, Instagram or Telegram wants.
image-social.title: Social Media Image Resizer — YouTube, Instagram, Telegram sizes
image-social.description: Free online resizer for social media. Crop and export at the exact pixel size for a YouTube thumbnail, Instagram post or story, Telegram channel photo, X header and more. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
image-social.intro: Pick where the picture is going and the frame locks to that shape. Drag it to choose what stays in shot, then save at the exact pixel size the platform asks for. If the whole picture has to fit — a logo, or a tall photo in a wide banner — switch to keeping it all and fill the sides with a blurred copy of itself.

howTo.step1: Add the picture you want to post.
howTo.step2: Pick the platform and size, then drag the frame over the part that matters.
howTo.step3: Press Make the image and download it.

faq.q1: Why does the size matter?
faq.a1: Every platform re-crops anything that arrives at the wrong shape, and it crops from the centre without looking — which is how titles lose their last word and group photos lose the person on the end. Sending the picture already at the right shape is the only way to decide what stays in frame yourself.
faq.q2: What is the difference between filling and keeping the whole picture?
faq.a2: Filling cuts the picture down to the shape needed, so nothing is left over but something is lost off the edges. Keeping it all leaves the picture whole and puts something either side — a blurred blow-up of the picture itself, which is what video apps do and reads as deliberate, or plain white or black. Use filling for photos, keeping for logos and screenshots where an edge matters.
faq.q3: My picture is smaller than the size I picked.
faq.a3: It will be enlarged, and enlarging cannot add detail that was never captured, so it will look a little soft. For a thumbnail it usually still passes; for a 2560-pixel-wide channel banner it will not. Start from the largest copy you have — the original off the camera rather than one already posted and re-compressed somewhere.
faq.a4: JPG for photographs — it is what every platform re-encodes to anyway. PNG for logos, screenshots and anything with flat colour or sharp text, where JPG leaves a halo. WebP is smaller than both but not every upload form accepts it, so use it for your own website rather than for a post.
faq.a5: No. The crop and the resize happen inside your browser, on your own device — nothing is sent to a server, and the picture reaches the internet only when you post it yourself.

image-favicon.name: Favicon generator
image-favicon.short: Turn a logo into favicon.ico and every icon a site needs.
image-favicon.title: Favicon Generator — make favicon.ico from PNG or SVG, free
image-favicon.description: Free favicon generator. Turn a PNG, JPG or SVG into favicon.ico plus the apple-touch-icon and manifest icons a site needs, in one zip. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
image-favicon.intro: Add a logo, choose the square that matters, and get favicon.ico with 16, 32 and 48 pixel versions inside it, the PNGs modern browsers and phones look for, a ready site.webmanifest, and the three lines of HTML to paste. Every size is drawn from the original at that size, not shrunk from one big one.

howTo.step1: Add a logo — PNG, JPG or SVG.
howTo.step2: Drag the square over the part that should be the icon and set the background.
howTo.step3: Press Make the favicon set and unzip the files into your site's root folder.

faq.q1: Why is favicon.ico not just one image?
faq.a1: Because it is a container. A browser reads the file and picks the size closest to what it needs — 16 px for the tab, 32 px on a bookmark bar, 48 px for a Windows shortcut. If only one large image is inside, the browser shrinks it itself, and browsers are bad at that: fine lines and small text turn to mush at 16 px. Each size here is drawn separately from your original.
faq.q2: Do I still need favicon.ico if I have PNGs?
faq.a2: Yes, and it costs nothing to include. Browsers still ask for /favicon.ico by name even when no tag points at it, and some older ones read nothing else. The PNGs cover modern browsers, the iPhone home screen and Android's install prompt — which is why all of them are in the zip.
faq.a3: For the tab icon, usually yes: it then sits properly on both light and dark browser themes. The exception is the iPhone home-screen icon, which Apple composites onto black — so that one is given a solid background automatically even when you pick transparent, because a dark logo on black is invisible.
faq.a4: Yes, and it gives the best result. The SVG is drawn fresh at each size rather than rasterised once and scaled, so the 16 px icon is a real 16 px rendering. Everything works in your browser, so the SVG never leaves your device.
faq.a5: All of them in the root folder of your site — the same level as index.html — so they are reachable at /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png. Then paste the three lines from the zip's how-to-use.txt into the head section of your pages. If the old icon sticks around, that is the browser's cache; a hard refresh usually clears it.

svg-to-png.name: SVG to PNG
svg-to-png.short: Turn a vector into a picture at any size you need.
svg-to-png.title: SVG to PNG — convert vector to image online, free, no upload
svg-to-png.description: Free SVG to PNG converter. Draw a vector at any size — 1×, 2×, 4× or an exact width — with transparency kept. Runs in your browser, so it renders exactly as a web page would.
svg-to-png.intro: Add an SVG and pick how big the picture should be. Because the drawing happens in your own browser, the result is exactly what that SVG looks like on a web page — not another engine's guess at it. Transparency is kept unless you ask for JPG, which has none.

howTo.step1: Add an SVG file.
howTo.step2: Choose a multiple of its own size, or type an exact width.
howTo.step3: Press Convert and download the picture.

faq.q1: What size should I pick?
faq.a1: Whatever the picture will be shown at, then double it if it is going on a screen — a 2× image looks sharp on the high-resolution displays most phones and laptops now have. There is no upper limit worth respecting other than file size: a vector has no resolution of its own, so 4× is as sharp as 1×.
faq.q2: Why is my SVG coming out the wrong size?
faq.a2: Many SVGs are exported with only a viewBox and no width or height, so they have no size of their own and the default here is taken from that viewBox. Type an exact width instead and the proportions are kept from the same source, which is usually what you wanted.
faq.q3: Will fonts and effects look right?
faq.a3: The browser draws it, so anything that works on a web page works here — gradients, filters, clipping. The one exception is text set in a font your device does not have: the browser substitutes another, exactly as it would on a page. Converting text to outlines in your drawing program before exporting avoids that for good.
faq.q4: Can I go back from PNG to SVG?
faq.a4: Not meaningfully. A vector is a set of instructions and a PNG is a grid of pixels; turning the grid back into instructions is tracing, and it guesses. Keep the SVG as your original and export PNGs from it whenever you need one.
faq.a5: No. The SVG is read and drawn inside your browser, on your own device. It is also loaded in a way that runs no scripts and fetches nothing, so an SVG from an unknown source cannot do anything while it is being converted.

image-watermark.name: Add watermark
image-watermark.short: Put your name or logo on a picture before you share it.
image-watermark.title: Add Watermark to Photo — free, online, no upload
image-watermark.description: Free online watermark tool. Add text or a logo to a picture, anywhere on it or repeated across the whole thing, and save. Runs in your browser — the picture is never uploaded.
image-watermark.intro: Type your name or add a logo, place it where you want, and set how strongly it shows. The preview is the real thing, so what you line up is what gets saved. For anything you expect to be lifted, repeat the mark across the whole picture — a corner mark is one crop away from gone.

howTo.step1: Add the picture you are about to share.
howTo.step2: Type your text or add a logo, then place it and set the strength.
howTo.step3: Press Save watermarked and download it.

faq.q1: Where should I put the mark?
faq.a1: A mark in a corner is tidy and easy to crop off, which is fine if you only want people to know who made something. If you are protecting work that gets lifted — a photographer's proofs, a listing photo — repeat it across the whole picture at low opacity. Removing that means removing it from every part of the image, which is far more trouble than finding another photo.
faq.a2: Strong enough to be unmistakable, faint enough not to ruin the picture — around half opacity is usually the balance. White works on most photographs because it survives dark and light areas alike; black disappears into shadows. Turning it a little off horizontal makes it harder to paint out cleanly.
faq.a3: A determined person with editing software can remove most of them, and tools that do it automatically exist. The point is not to be impossible — it is to be more work than it is worth, and to make an unmarked copy obviously stolen when one turns up. A repeated, semi-transparent mark over the subject achieves that; a small corner logo does not.
faq.a4: The picture is saved again in the same format at high quality, which costs a very small amount on a JPG as any re-save does, and nothing at all on PNG or WebP. The mark itself is drawn into the pixels, so it survives being screenshotted, re-saved and re-posted.
faq.a5: No. Both the picture and the logo stay in your browser, on your own device. Nothing is sent to a server — which matters here, because unwatermarked originals are exactly what you are trying not to hand out.

image-join.name: Join images
image-join.short: Put several pictures together into one.
image-join.title: Combine Images Into One — free, online, no upload
image-join.description: Free online tool to join pictures into one image — side by side, stacked, or in a grid, with an optional gap. Runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.
image-join.intro: Add the pictures, drag them into the order you want, and choose whether they sit side by side, one above another, or in a grid. Pictures in a row are brought to a common height and pictures in a column to a common width, so the join is a straight line rather than a staircase.

howTo.step1: Add two or more pictures.
howTo.step2: Drag them into order and pick an arrangement.
howTo.step3: Press Join them and download the single image.

faq.q1: What happens if the pictures are different sizes?
faq.a1: In a row they are all brought to the same height, in a column to the same width. The common size is the smallest of them, because matching upwards would enlarge pictures past the detail they hold and make the whole thing look soft. Nothing is cropped.
faq.q2: Why does the grid leave space around some pictures?
faq.a2: Because every cell is the same and each picture is fitted inside it whole. A collage app would crop to fill the cell instead, which looks tidier but silently cuts the edges off — and the edge is often where the thing you were photographing is. Set the gap colour to match and the spacing reads as deliberate.
faq.q3: How many pictures can I join?
faq.a3: As many as your device can hold in memory at once. The result gets large quickly — eight phone photos side by side is a very wide image — so if you plan to send it anywhere, run it through Compress image afterwards.
faq.q4: Can I put text or borders between them?
faq.a4: Not here. Set a gap and a gap colour for a plain border; for anything more, join them first and add the text in whatever you would normally use. Keeping this tool to one job is what makes it predictable.
faq.a5: No. They are read and drawn together inside your browser, on your own device. Nothing is sent to a server.

image-split.name: Split image
image-split.short: Cut one picture into a grid of pieces.
image-split.title: Split Image Into Grid — 3x3 for Instagram, free, online
image-split.description: Free online image splitter. Cut a picture into a grid — 3×3 for an Instagram layout, or any rows and columns — and download the pieces in one zip. Runs in your browser.
image-split.intro: Choose how many rows and columns, see the cut lines on the picture, and get every piece in one zip. The pieces are named by row and column, so putting them back in the right order later is not a guessing game.

howTo.step1: Add the picture you want to cut up.
howTo.step2: Pick a grid — 3 × 3 is the Instagram layout — or set rows and columns yourself.
howTo.step3: Press Cut it up and download the zip.

faq.q1: How do I post a 3 × 3 grid on Instagram?
faq.a1: Upload the pieces in reverse reading order — bottom right first, top left last — because the newest post sits at the top left of a profile. The files are named row-column for exactly this reason: 3-3 goes up first, then 3-2, and so on to 1-1.
faq.a2: The picture's size divided by the grid, with any leftover pixels given to the last row and column rather than thrown away, so the pieces still add up to the original exactly. Start from a large picture: a 1080-pixel square cut into nine is 360 pixels a piece, which is on the soft side for a phone screen.
faq.q3: Should I crop it square first?
faq.a3: For a profile grid, yes — Instagram shows squares, and a rectangle cut into nine gives nine rectangles that will be cropped again on the way in. Crop image will square it up first, and then the grid comes out as intended.
faq.a4: A single zip containing every piece as a separate file, in the same format as the picture you added. Unzip it and the files sort themselves into reading order by name.
faq.a5: No. It is cut inside your browser, on your own device, and the zip is assembled there too.

image-filters.name: Black and white
image-filters.short: Turn a picture monochrome, or adjust brightness and contrast.
image-filters.title: Black and White Photo — convert and adjust online, free
image-filters.description: Free online tool to make a picture black and white or sepia, and to adjust brightness, contrast and colour. Runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
image-filters.intro: Pick a look — black and white, sepia, or the high-contrast setting that makes a photographed document readable — or move the three sliders yourself. The preview shows the real result, and the adjustment is applied to the pixels when you save, so it survives being sent anywhere.

howTo.step1: Add a picture.
howTo.step2: Choose a look or set brightness, contrast and colour yourself.
howTo.step3: Press Save adjusted and download it.

faq.q1: Why would I make a photo black and white?
faq.a1: Documents, mostly. A photographed page in black and white with strong contrast reads far better than the yellowish original, and the file is smaller. For photographs it is a matter of taste — removing colour puts the attention on shape and light, which flatters some pictures and ruins others.
faq.q2: What is the Scanned document setting?
faq.a2: Black and white with the brightness lifted and the contrast pushed hard, which turns a grey photograph of a page into something closer to a scan: the paper goes white, the text goes black, and the shadow from your hand mostly disappears. Take the photo as square-on and evenly lit as you can first — this cleans up a decent photo, it does not rescue a bad one.
faq.a3: Not from the saved file. The adjustment is applied to the pixels, which is what makes it show up everywhere rather than only in the app that made it — so keep your original. Nothing here changes the file you added; you get a new one.
faq.a4: The picture is saved again in the same format at high quality, which costs a very small amount on a JPG as any re-save does, and nothing on PNG or WebP. Strong contrast can flatten detail in the darkest and lightest parts, so ease off if shadows start turning into solid black.
faq.a5: No. The adjustment happens inside your browser, on your own device — which is worth knowing when the thing you are photographing is a document.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Toolkave does and does not collect. Your files are processed in your browser and never uploaded.
privacy.lead: The short version: your files never leave your device. There is no account, no upload, and nothing for us to lose.

sections.heading: What happens to your files
body: Every tool on this site runs inside your browser. When you choose a PDF or a photo, it is read into your browser's memory and processed there by JavaScript and WebAssembly that has already been downloaded to your device. The file is never sent to us, because there is no server to send it to — the site is a set of static files.
When you close the tab, the file is gone. We cannot recover it, produce it in response to a legal request, or lose it in a breach, because we never had it.
You can verify this yourself: open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab, and run any tool. You will see no upload.

sections.heading: The Telegram bot is the exception
body: Our Telegram bot, {'@'}toolkavebot, cannot work the same way. A file you send it goes to Telegram's servers first, and our code then downloads it to convert it. That is how every Telegram bot works.

While converting, the file is held in memory only. It is never written to a disk, a database or a storage bucket, and it is discarded the moment the PDF is sent back. We keep only the Telegram identifiers needed to count the files in your current batch, and those are deleted when the batch finishes or after a day of inactivity.
Anything you send through Telegram is also covered by Telegram's own privacy policy.

sections.heading: What we measure
body: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics to see which pages are visited. It sets no cookies, does not fingerprint your browser, and does not build a profile of you. It records aggregate figures: page views, country, referring site, and how quickly pages load.
Like every website, our host also keeps short-lived request logs — IP address, browser, and URL requested — which Cloudflare uses to serve the site and to block abuse.

sections.heading: Cookies and local storage
body: We set no cookies.

One tool stores something on your device: the currency converter saves the day's exchange rates in your browser's local storage so it does not have to fetch them again. That data stays on your machine and contains nothing about you. Clearing your browser data removes it.

sections.heading: Other services
body: The site is hosted by Cloudflare, which serves the pages and provides the analytics described above.
Fonts are served from this domain rather than a font network, so loading a page contacts nobody else.

Two tools reach outside on purpose: the currency converter fetches rates from the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (cbu.uz) and open.er-api.com, and the YouTube thumbnail tool loads images from YouTube. Those requests carry the video ID or currency you asked about, nothing more.

sections.heading: Advertising
body: The site currently shows no ads and contains no advertising or tracking scripts. If that changes, this page will be updated before any ad code goes live, and it will say plainly what the ad network can see.

sections.heading: Your rights, and children
body: We hold no personal data about you, so there is nothing to export, correct or delete. If you believe otherwise, write to us and we will look into it.
The site is not directed at children and collects nothing from anyone.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
body: If this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it.
Questions about privacy: hello{'@'}toolkave.com

body: A set of tools that run in your browser, offered free of charge and as they are. There is no subscription, no usage limit, and no promise that any particular tool will still be here next year.

body: We claim no rights over anything you process here. On the website we never receive your files at all, so the question mostly does not arise; through the Telegram bot we hold them only for the seconds it takes to convert them.

Keep your originals, and check anything that matters before you rely on it. We are not liable for loss or damage arising from using the site, to the extent the law allows.

Because everything runs on your own device, we have no way to police this and no wish to. The responsibility is yours.

about.title: About Toolkave
about.description: Why Toolkave exists: everyday file tools that work without uploading your documents to anyone.
about.lead: Toolkave is a set of everyday file tools that run entirely in your browser. It exists because handing a private document to a stranger's server for a ten-second job never made sense.

sections.heading: The problem
body: Merging two PDFs, converting photos of a document, removing a password you already know — these take seconds of computing. Yet almost every site that offers them asks you to upload the file, wait while it is processed on someone else's machine, and trust that it is deleted afterwards.
Passports, contracts, medical results and bank statements go through those sites every day.

sections.heading: How this is different
body: Browsers can do this work themselves now. Every tool here runs on your own device: the file is read into memory, processed, and handed straight back to you. Nothing is uploaded, so nothing can be kept, leaked or subpoenaed.
It also means the tools work on a slow connection and keep working once the page has loaded.

sections.heading: Three languages, on purpose
body: Toolkave is built in Uzbek, Russian and English. Good tools in Uzbek are rare, and translating an interface is not the same as writing one — every page here is written in each language rather than run through a translator.

sections.heading: Open and independent
body: The project is independent, built and maintained in Uzbekistan, and the source is public on GitHub. If you want to know exactly what a tool does with your file, you can read it.

sections.heading: What is next
body: More tools — images, text, converters and calculators — and a Telegram bot for the jobs that are easier from a phone. If something you need is missing, say so; that is how most of this list was chosen.

sections.heading: GitHub
body: The source lives at github.com/doniyorerkinov/toolkave. Issues and pull requests are welcome.

sections.heading: Reporting a bug well
body: If a tool gave you a wrong result, tell us which tool, which browser, and what the file was like — how many pages, roughly how large, whether it was scanned or made on a computer.
Please do not send the file itself unless we ask. It usually is not needed, and we would rather not have it.
